variants.title: Give each part its job
variants.context: A computer vision system turns pixels from images or video into a product decision: identify an object, follow it over time, measure a condition, retrieve similar media, or raise an alert. The model is one stage in a larger path that captures media, decodes and transforms frames, schedules accelerator work, applies temporal and business rules, and records evidence.
variants.prompt: From the lesson section “Start with the decision, not the model name”: match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Image classification
pairs.detail: Return a class or embedding for an independent image.
pairs.explanation: Return a class or embedding for an independent image. Throughput and batching often matter more than frame-to-frame state.

pairs.label: Object detection
pairs.detail: Locate multiple objects, then apply confidence filtering and class-aware duplicate suppression before downstream use.
pairs.explanation: Locate multiple objects, then apply confidence filtering and class-aware duplicate suppression before downstream use.

pairs.label: Video tracking
pairs.explanation: Associate detections across frames. Sampling too sparsely can break identity continuity even when per-frame detection remains accurate.

variants.hint: Give each part the one job only it can do, then rule out the rest. If accelerator serving and compression are new, review Real-time ML inference and Model compression techniques first.
variants.explanation: Each part has a distinct responsibility. Image classification: Return a class or embedding for an independent image. Object detection: Locate multiple objects, then apply confidence filtering and class-aware duplicate suppression before downstream use. Video tracking: Associate detections across frames.

variants.prompt: From the lesson section “Design failure modes before they happen”: match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Camera or decoder failure
pairs.detail: Detect frozen frames, timestamp gaps, codec errors, and source authentication failures.
pairs.explanation: Detect frozen frames, timestamp gaps, codec errors, and source authentication failures. Mark the source unavailable rather than returning a confident result from stale media.

pairs.label: Accelerator loss
pairs.detail: Stop admitting low-priority work, route compatible models to another pool, and protect queue age.
pairs.explanation: Stop admitting low-priority work, route compatible models to another pool, and protect queue age. Test the fleet against the largest planned failure domain.

pairs.label: Transform mismatch
pairs.detail: Fail a golden-tensor check or version gate before serving.
pairs.explanation: Fail a golden-tensor check or version gate before serving. Roll back model and transform together rather than changing one side of the contract.

pairs.label: Distribution shift
pairs.detail: Compare input and confidence distributions by named slice, sample uncertain media for labeling, and narrow authority until outcome evidence is available.
pairs.explanation: Compare input and confidence distributions by named slice, sample uncertain media for labeling, and narrow authority until outcome evidence is available.

variants.prompt: What is the core freshness invariant for an admitted live-video frame?

It must be retained forever
